extracted.intended_audience: museum/gallery visitors, photojournalism students, journalists, and the general public interested in press ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for ethical practice in news/photojournalism centered on photographic authenticity, captioning, attribution, and editorial accountability; illustrated by a case of digital manipulation. Useful for photographers, editors, and students learning standards for publishing documentary images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic authenticity / no deceptive compositing
rubrics_metrics.description: The published photo is a composite of two images taken seconds apart; the photographer confessed to having digitally merged the two photographs to improve the composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News photographs should not be digitally merged or composited to create a scene that did not occur as presented; manipulating images to change who appears, where they are, or how they relate is a breach of editorial standards and undermines the photograph's truth value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the newspaper's code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Walski was immediately fired for violating the newspaper’s code of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers and editors must follow their publication's written ethics policies (which typically prohibit fabrication or deceptive alteration of news images). Violations can result in disciplinary action, up to termination, and require public remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate captioning and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The caption published in the March 31, 2003 Los Angeles Times reads: “Warning: A British soldier manning the Azubayr Bridge orders fleeing Basra residents to hit the dirt as Iraqi forces open fire.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions must accurately describe what the image shows and its context; a caption that asserts actions or relationships not actually present in the unaltered photo misleads readers and compounds ethical breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and correction when manipulation is discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: Walski apologized to the Times; the Los Angeles Times Editor’s Note and coverage (Poynter article) followed the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an alteration or error is discovered, publications should issue transparent corrections/explanations (editor's notes, apologies) and provide the facts of the breach to restore accountability and inform readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution and crediting of images
rubrics_metrics.description: First published on the front of The Los Angeles Times, the image also ran in the Chicago Tribune and the Hartford Courant. Image copyright Brian Walski.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images must be properly credited to their creators and publications; provenance and copyright information should be preserved and published to maintain transparency about source and ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulating images to manufacture emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The widely published image ... seems to show the soldier gesturing at the civilians – urging them to seek cover – as a standing man holding a young child in his arms seems to look at the soldier imploringly. It’s the kind of picture that wins a Pulitzer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers and editors should not alter images to intensify, invent, or misrepresent emotional narratives or dramatic composition intended to sway readers; creating scenes that 'win awards' by fabrication is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal verification and cross-publication scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Hartford Courant published the image, a Courant employee noticed a duplication of civilians in the background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications and peers should perform verification and vigilant editorial review (including comparing versions and looking for duplication/artifacts) to detect manipulation before and after publication; cross-publication scrutiny can reveal issues missed by an individual outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear distinction between representation and reality in editorial displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings 'REPRESENTATION' and 'REALITY' show the difference between what was presented and what actually happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial presentations of documentary images should clearly distinguish how an image was represented (caption/context) from the factual reality of how it was created; when misrepresentation occurs, separating representation from reality helps educate readers on the breach.
